gap: No result ChatGPT got works out that with the same pair of 400 W panels (EcoFlow's FAQ example: 37.1 V open-circuit, 12.9 A each), only the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus can take both: one panel per input gives 800 W and a refill in 1,024 / 800 = 1.28 h. Wired either way, the pair falls outside the stated input limits of the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 and the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2: in series 74.2 V is over the 60 V maximum, and in parallel 25.8 A is over 14.5 A (Anker) or 20 A (BLUETTI).
standout_why: Compared against the cited pages that opened (ankersolix.com/a1765 and ecoflow.com/us/delta-3-series-portable-power-station) and two results that were not cited (the EcoFlow DELTA 3 / DELTA 3 Plus FAQ and powerstations.reviews' Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 page). The cited pages give only maximum input wattage and the makers' claims ('Full Charge in 70 Minutes', 'recharge fully in just 1.8 hours'). The EcoFlow FAQ checks two 400 W panels against the single-input DELTA 3 only. powerstations.reviews checks series and parallel wiring for Jackery only. None of them puts one pair of panels against every candidate's voltage and current limits. The cited solargenreview.com review returned HTTP 429 and the cited REI manual returned HTTP 403, so I could not check those two.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's pick, the DELTA 3 Plus, for the stated question, and it rules out the strongest-looking alternative. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 makes the same '1,000W … Full in 70 Minutes' claim at $499, but it has one 12–60 V, 20 A input. Two common 400 W panels go over that limit in series and in parallel. A 1,000 W refill would need a single string working at 50 V or more (1,000 W / 20 A) while staying at or under 60 V open-circuit. With two panels, the fastest refill of the five candidates is the DELTA 3 Plus with one panel on each input.

findings.label: Refill hours with two 400 W panels, one per input
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus | EcoFlow Product FAQs | EcoFlow US
findings.note: Each input: 37.1 V ≤ 60 V and 12.9 A ≤ 15 A, so it passes. Total 2 × 400 W = 800 W; 1,024 Wh / 800 W = 1.28 h at the panels' rated output, before charging losses.

findings.label: Refill hours at the full 1,000 W input
findings.note: 1,024 Wh / 1,000 W = 1.02 h. Reaching this needs two panels of 500 W, each working at 33.3 V or more (500 W / 15 A) and staying within 60 V open-circuit and 15 A. EcoFlow claims 70 min.

findings.label: Refill hours, one 500 W input

findings.note: 1,024 Wh / 500 W = 2.05 h. The EcoFlow FAQ says two 400 W panels cannot be used: series 37.1 × 2 = 74.2 V gives 957 W, over the 500 W limit; parallel 12.9 × 2 = 25.8 A, over the 15 A limit. EcoFlow's series page says '500W MPPT recharges in 2 hours'.
